title: On Taiwan, US ‘Strategic Ambiguity’ Is Not Dead Yet
author: Denny Roy
text:
U.S. President Donald Trump delivers remarks at a press conference at Mar-a-Lago in Palm Beach, Florida, Jan. 3, 2026.
Credit: Official White House Photo by Molly Riley
Under the longstanding policy of “strategic ambiguity,” the U.S. government has refused to say ahead of time whether or not it would send American forces to help defend Taiwan against an attack from China. Some analysts say the Trump administration has rendered this policy ineffective by generating doubt that U.S. forces would intervene.To cite just one example, the title of a September 14 analysis by columnist James Crabtree in Foreign Policy proclaimed that “Trump is killing ‘strategic ambiguity’ over Taiwan.” Crabtree argued that based on “signals from Washington,” the United States is “inching more toward a position of nonintervention.” Similarly, geopolitical risk analyst Shahn Louis said “the era” of strategic ambiguity “is over.”  Michael Schiffer, a former U.S. deputy assistant secretary of defense for East Asia, argued that “strategic ambiguity is no longer a sustainable or effective policy.” [...]
